definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi).
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

There exist Csm>0 and tausm>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every smooth real mean-zero initial datum u_0 with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tausm, the exact solution u and unfiltered numerical trajectory satisfy sup_(0<=t<=T)||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma and max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma, where V is the interpolation of Interp at v^n=S_(-n*tau)u^n. All constants are uniform in the full stated smooth-data ball, Fourier support and higher norms.

output.statement: There exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0, the exact solution of KdV(u;u_0) exists with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning and the unfiltered recursion u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) satisfies max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Both constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball and independent of Fourier support and additional smoothness.

locals.declaration: Choose C=Csm from the common smooth bound F001.
Choose tau_0=tausm together with C from F001.
Take the exact solution of N001 for the current u_0 under L1.
useq_m is the unique N001 flow for u0seq_m.
unumseq_m is the Psi_tau recursion with datum u0seq_m.

argument.text: H001-H003 fix precisely T>0,0<gamma<=1,R>0. N011 supplies constants Csm,tausm valid simultaneously for every smooth real mean-zero datum in this H^gamma ball and every allowed number of steps. Record F001: such a common positive pair exists, depending only on T,gamma,R.

produces.statement: There exist C>0,tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that the grid bound C*tau^gamma holds for every smooth real mean-zero datum with H^gamma norm <=R and every positive Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0.

argument.text: Choose that common pair C,tau_0 before fixing arbitrary u_0,Lsteps. Assume L1: u_0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma with norm <=R, Lsteps is a positive integer and tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0. Since T>0, this tau is positive. N001 supplies its unique exact solution u with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning. Define u0seq_m=Ple_m u_0. Each is a real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, its H^gamma norm is <=R, and ||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 tends to zero by convergence of the Fourier norm tails. Thus F001 applies to every approximating datum with exactly these C,tau_0.

produces.statement: Under L1, u0seq_m is smooth real mean-zero, has H^gamma norm <=R, converges to u_0 in L^2, and the same C,tau_0 smooth grid estimate applies for every m.

argument.text: Let useq_m be the exact flows and unumseq_m their numerical trajectories. N001's L^2 continuous dependence, since the initial L^2 norms sum to <=2*R, gives sup_[0,T]||useq_m-u||_2<=K(T,2*R)||u0seq_m-u_0||_2 ->0. For this fixed tau and finite Lsteps, N007 makes every iterate of the unmodified update continuous on real mean-zero L^2. Inducting over n=0,...,Lsteps gives unumseq_m^n -> u^n in L^2 at every grid point. No uniform Lipschitz bound for Psi as tau->0 is required: the limit is taken at a fixed timestep, with finite 1/tau coefficients and finitely many iterations.

produces.statement: Under L1, useq_m -> u uniformly in L^2 on [0,T], and unumseq_m^n -> u^n in L^2 at every one of the finitely many grid points.

argument.text: For each m, F002 yields max_n||useq_m(n*tau)-unumseq_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Use F003 and continuity of the norm, and then take the maximum over the finite Lsteps+1 points, to pass to the limit. This gives max_n||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. The exact solution is the unique smooth-approximation solution by N001; N007 ensures the rough-data recursion is defined and stays real mean-zero. The constants C,tau_0 are unchanged in this limit and were chosen uniformly before u_0,Lsteps. Discharge L1 and introduce both universal quantifiers. P follows for the entire original ball, with no Fourier support or extra smoothness hypothesis.
